name: Vancouver
title: Pixel Light Shows in Vancouver, BC
description: Music-reactive mega trees, rooflines and wrapped trees for Vancouver businesses, BIAs and civic sites, sealed for coastal rain. Kits, install and software.
intro: Vancouver's winter is dark early and wet far more often than it is white, which makes it one of the best cities in Canada for permanent pixel lighting. Rooflines and wrapped trees can stay up all year and change theme with the calendar, and a mega tree in a plaza or courtyard draws people out on a rainy December evening.
climate: Winters on the coast are mild, usually hovering a few degrees above freezing, with long runs of rain and the occasional wet snowfall that rarely lasts. The challenge is water rather than cold: weeks of steady rain find any connector that is not sealed, and wind off the water drives it sideways.
installNotes: Every pixel connection is sealed and every cable gets a drip loop so water runs off before it reaches a joint.
Controller and power enclosures are mounted under cover where possible, with cable glands at the bottom, never the top.
Near the water we use corrosion-resistant clips and fasteners and check them at each service visit.
Because roofs rarely ice up, rooflines are good candidates for year-round permanent installs with theme changes through the seasons.
districts: Commercial activity in Vancouver is spread across the downtown core and dozens of neighbourhood high streets, each with its own character and, in many cases, its own business improvement association running seasonal events. Courtyards, plazas, hotel entrances and waterfront promenades are natural homes for a mega tree, while street trees along a high street suit wrapped-tree programs coordinated with the association and the city.
season: Sunset comes before 4:30 pm in December, so a scheduled show can run from late afternoon through the evening rush. Book in late summer for a November install; permanent rooflines can go in any time of year.
recommendWhy: A Business Kit mega tree is the quickest win for a single frontage; add a year-round roofline and wrapped trees on the same controller.

faqs.question: Will the lights survive Vancouver rain?
faqs.answer: Yes, if they are installed for it. We seal every connection, add drip loops, mount enclosures with bottom-entry glands and check the run at each service visit. Rain is the main design factor on the coast, not cold.

faqs.question: Can we leave a roofline up all year in Vancouver?
faqs.answer: Usually, yes. Mild winters with little roof ice make permanent rooflines practical. The Light Show app's schedule turns them on at dusk, and you change themes for holidays, events or your brand colours.

name: Victoria
title: Pixel Light Shows in Victoria, BC
description: Music-reactive pixel lighting for Victoria hotels, heritage streets and civic spaces: mega trees, rooflines and wrapped trees, with lifetime software access.
intro: Victoria has the mildest winter climate of any major Canadian city, a compact heritage downtown and a harbour that people walk all year. That combination suits permanent rooflines and wrapped trees that change theme through the seasons, with a sequenced holiday show at the centre of it.
climate: Winters are cool and damp rather than cold, with rain, coastal wind and salt air, and snow that is rare and short-lived. Like Vancouver, the enemy is moisture and corrosion, and exposed waterfront sites take the brunt of winter storms.
installNotes: Sealed connections, drip loops and bottom-entry enclosures for long wet spells.
Corrosion-resistant hardware on waterfront and harbour-facing sites.
On heritage facades we favour clip and clamp mounts that avoid drilling into original masonry, and we work with your heritage requirements before anything is fixed.
Wind-rated anchoring for mega trees on open, exposed sites.
districts: Downtown Victoria is a walkable mix of heritage blocks, the inner harbour, Chinatown and independent retail streets, with tourism and hospitality setting much of the seasonal rhythm. Hotels, restaurants and retail courtyards are typical commercial clients, and downtown business groups and the municipality are natural partners for streetscape and tree-wrap programs.
season: Short December days and a year-round visitor season mean a display earns its keep beyond the holidays. Plan a summer site walk for a late-autumn install.
recommendWhy: A mega tree gives visitors a holiday focal point; permanent rooflines and wrapped trees can be added to the same controller for year-round colour.

faqs.question: Can you install on a heritage building in Victoria?
faqs.answer: Yes. We plan mounts that clip or clamp to existing features rather than drilling into original masonry where possible, and we work to your heritage requirements and approvals before installation.

faqs.question: Is travel to Vancouver Island extra?
faqs.answer: Victoria is in our BC & Ontario travel zone, so a crew trip fee applies, plus accommodation on multi-day installs. Your quote confirms the travel figure for the island.

name: Kelowna
title: Pixel Light Shows in Kelowna, BC
description: Music-reactive pixel lighting for Kelowna and Okanagan wineries, resorts and downtown businesses: mega trees, rooflines and wrapped trees, installed for you.
h1: Music-reactive pixel lighting for Kelowna and the Okanagan
intro: Kelowna's draw is the lake, the wineries and the resorts, and its winters are often grey under valley cloud. A display that lights up a winery entrance, a resort plaza or the downtown waterfront gives people a reason to come out on the long evenings between the summer and ski seasons.
climate: The Okanagan is drier than the coast, with cold winters, moderate snow and frequent low cloud trapped in the valley. Summers are hot and sunny, so anything left up year-round has to handle strong UV as well as winter freeze-thaw.
installNotes: UV-stable cable, clips and pixel housings for permanent installs that see a full Okanagan summer.
Freeze-thaw rated sealing at every connection.
Snow and wind anchoring for mega trees on open vineyard and resort sites.
Long data and power runs planned carefully on large rural properties.
districts: Commercial lighting in the area centres on the downtown waterfront and its business association, resort and hotel properties, wineries along the lake benches, and suburban retail centres. Rural sites often mean long runs between the building and the feature tree, which we design for at the site walk.
season: Book early autumn for a holiday install; wineries and resorts often want the display ready for November events.
recommendWhy: A mega tree at the tasting room or lodge entrance, with rooflines and wrapped trees along the drive added on the same controller as budget allows.

faqs.question: Do you install at wineries and resorts outside Kelowna?
faqs.answer: Yes. Installation is available anywhere in the Okanagan and across Canada; travel is charged by zone, and long runs on rural properties are planned at the site walk.

faqs.question: Can the display react to live music at events?
faqs.answer: Yes. The controller's USB microphone listens to whatever is playing, and the quiet-room gate keeps the lights resting on a soft glow when the music stops.

name: Calgary
title: Pixel Light Shows in Calgary, AB
description: Music-reactive mega trees, rooflines and wrapped trees for Calgary businesses, BIAs and civic sites, installed to handle chinooks and deep cold snaps.
intro: Calgary winters swing hard: a chinook can lift the temperature well above freezing in a few hours, and a cold snap can drop it below minus thirty a few days later. Pixel lighting that lives through that cycle is installed differently from lighting that only has to survive a mild season.
climate: The air is dry, the sun is strong at Calgary's elevation, and chinook winds bring rapid thaws followed by hard refreezes. Those repeated freeze-thaw cycles work on fasteners, sealant and anything that traps water, and deep cold makes cable stiff and brittle.
installNotes: Mounts and clips that tolerate repeated freeze-thaw without loosening, checked at each service visit.
Connections sealed so meltwater from a chinook cannot sit in a joint and freeze.
Cold-flexible cable and service loops so stiff cable in a cold snap does not pull on connectors.
Wind-rated anchoring for mega trees; chinook gusts can be strong.
districts: Calgary's commercial lighting opportunities range from the downtown core and inner-city main streets, many with their own BIA running seasonal programming, to large suburban retail centres, hotels and event venues. Plazas and pedestrian streets suit mega trees, while main-street BIAs often phase in rooflines block by block.
season: Install before mid-November to avoid working through the coldest stretches; shows run on a dusk schedule from the first week of December.
recommendWhy: Main-street BIAs and retail centres get the most from two mega trees with wrapped trees and arches where people walk, adding rooflines in later phases.

faqs.question: How do chinooks affect pixel lighting?
faqs.answer: The rapid thaw and refreeze is harder on hardware than steady cold. We seal connections against meltwater, use clips that hold through freeze-thaw and check fasteners at every service visit.

faqs.question: What does travel to Calgary cost?
faqs.answer: Calgary is in our Prairies zone: a crew trip fee from Saskatchewan plus accommodation on multi-day installs. The budget planner on this page shows the figures for your layout.

name: Edmonton
title: Pixel Light Shows in Edmonton, AB
description: Music-reactive pixel lighting for Edmonton businesses, BIAs and civic spaces: mega trees, rooflines and wrapped trees installed for long, cold winters.
intro: Edmonton has long, cold, dark winters and a city that makes the most of them, with winter patios, festivals and outdoor events through the season. A synchronised light show gives a plaza, a main street or a venue entrance something to gather around from late afternoon on.
climate: Expect extended stretches well below minus twenty, dry air and early sunsets, around 4:15 pm in December. Snow is steady rather than heavy, and the cold is the main design factor: cable stiffens, plastic becomes brittle and anything installed has to stay put for months without attention.
installNotes: Installs scheduled before the deep cold so crews are not handling stiff cable at minus thirty.
Cold-flexible cable and generous service loops at every connector.
Power supplies and controllers in enclosures sized for the load, mounted off the ground and clear of snow banks.
Long dark evenings mean long run times; the schedule turns the show on at dusk and off at close.
districts: Edmonton's opportunities include downtown and its BIAs, older main streets in neighbourhoods across the city, large retail centres, hotels and event venues. Main-street BIAs already invest in winter programming, and a synchronised show tying several storefronts together fits that well.
season: Book by early autumn; we aim to install in late October and early November ahead of the cold.
recommendWhy: Long winters reward a larger display: two mega trees, wrapped trees and walk-through arches running on a nightly schedule for months.

faqs.question: Do the lights work at minus thirty?
faqs.answer: The 12 V WS2811 pixels and controllers run in deep cold. What matters is installing before the cold, using cold-flexible cable and leaving slack so stiff cable never pulls on a connector.

faqs.question: Can the show run every night on its own?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Light Show app's schedule turns the lights on and off at set times on chosen days, and can start a playlist of looks and themes at the on time.

name: Québec City
title: Pixel Light Shows in Québec City, QC
description: Music-reactive pixel lighting for Québec City businesses and civic spaces, installed for heavy snow and heritage streets: mega trees, rooflines and more.
h1: Music-reactive pixel lighting for Québec City
intro: Québec City is one of the snowiest cities of its size anywhere, home to a UNESCO World Heritage old town and the Carnaval de Québec. Winter is the main event, and lighting that can live through it is worth investing in.
climate: Very heavy snowfall, long cold winters, wind off the St. Lawrence and freezing rain. Snow load and snow clearing shape every installation decision.
installNotes: Props, enclosures and cable runs placed above the expected snow line.
Mega trees anchored and braced for heavy snow load.
Heritage-sensitive clip and clamp mounts on historic stone buildings, planned with your approvals.
Cold-flexible cable; installs finished before the deep cold.
districts: Commercial streets, the old town, hotels and hospitality, retail centres and event venues all lean into winter. Heritage districts bring approval requirements that we build into the schedule.
season: Book in early summer; heritage approvals and travel need lead time.
recommendWhy: A long, snowy season rewards a larger synchronised display with mega trees, wrapped trees and walk-through arches.

faqs.question: Can lighting go up in a heritage district?
faqs.answer: Often, yes, with the right mounts and approvals. We avoid drilling original stone where possible and work to the requirements that apply to your building.

faqs.question: How do you handle heavy snow?
faqs.answer: We keep props, enclosures and cables above the snow line, brace mega trees for load and agree routes with whoever clears snow on the site.

name: Halifax
title: Pixel Light Shows in Halifax, NS
description: Music-reactive pixel lighting for Halifax businesses, business districts and the waterfront, built for coastal storms: mega trees, rooflines and wrapped trees.
intro: Halifax lives on its waterfront, and its downtown and neighbourhood business districts work year-round to bring people to the harbour and the main streets. A music-reactive display gives a winter evening on the boardwalk or a main street something to see.
climate: Maritime winters alternate between rain, snow and freezing rain, often in the same week, with strong coastal winds, nor'easters and salt air. Moisture, ice and wind matter more than deep cold.
installNotes: Corrosion-resistant hardware and sealed connections for salt air.
Wind-rated anchoring for storm conditions on the waterfront.
Drip loops and bottom-entry enclosures for mixed precipitation.
Service visits after major storms on request.
districts: Halifax's business districts, from downtown and the waterfront to neighbourhood main streets, run seasonal programming, and hotels, restaurants and retail along the harbour are natural clients for rooflines and feature trees.
season: Book in summer for a November install; Atlantic installs are scheduled early to fit travel and freight.
recommendWhy: A mega tree on the waterfront or at a venue entrance is a strong single feature; rooflines can follow on the same controller.

faqs.question: Will the display survive a nor'easter?
faqs.answer: It is installed for it: wind-rated anchors, secured cable runs, corrosion-resistant hardware and sealed connections. We can schedule a check after a major storm.

faqs.question: What does travel to Halifax cost?
faqs.answer: Halifax is in our Québec & Atlantic zone: a crew trip fee plus accommodation on multi-day installs. See the planner on this page for your layout.

name: St. John's
title: Pixel Light Shows in St. John's, NL
description: Music-reactive pixel lighting for St. John's businesses and downtown, built for wind, fog and freezing rain: mega trees, rooflines and wrapped trees, installed.
h1: Music-reactive pixel lighting for St. John's
intro: St. John's is famous for its colourful row houses climbing the hills above the harbour, for Water Street and for its weather. A display that reacts to music suits a downtown known for live music, as long as it is built for the wind.
climate: St. John's is often described as Canada's windiest, foggiest and wettest major city, with heavy snow, freezing rain and storms off the Atlantic. Wind and ice are the design factors.
installNotes: Everything anchored and secured along its full run; nothing left loose to whip in the wind.
Sealed connections and drip loops for fog, rain and freezing rain.
Corrosion-resistant hardware for salt air.
Freight and crew travel planned well ahead, with spare pixels left on site.
districts: Downtown St. John's, with its business improvement area, Water Street and the harbourfront, is the heart of the city's evenings out, alongside hotels, retail centres and venues. Steep streets and colourful facades make rooflines especially striking.
season: Book in early summer; Newfoundland installs are scheduled early for freight and travel.
recommendWhy: A mega tree is a strong first phase for a downtown block, with rooflines on the colourful facades added later on the same controller.

faqs.question: Can pixel lighting handle St. John's wind?
faqs.answer: Yes, when it is installed for it: wind-rated anchors and clips, cable secured along every run and props sized for the site. We assess exposure at the site walk.

faqs.question: Is travel to Newfoundland included?
faqs.answer: St. John's is in our Québec & Atlantic zone: a crew trip fee plus accommodation on multi-day installs, with freight planned ahead.
